critical_code_review_comments: sanitize.js — addHook('afterSanitizeAttributes', ...) is added at module load time. DOMPurify hooks are GLOBAL across all DOMPurify.sanitize() callers. safePreview.js registers the same hook again — so the same callback runs twice on every sanitize across the app. Functionally idempotent (setAttribute with same value), but worth deduping (register the hook once in a shared init module) to avoid surprise side effects when future configs diverge.

EmailComposerDialog renders 4 separate dangerouslySetInnerHTML blocks; each one re-sanitises on every render. Consider useMemo around sanitizeEmailHtml(...) keyed by the html prop to skip repeated DOMPurify work on unrelated re-renders.

openSafePdfPreview accepts only 'data:application/pdf;' prefix (note the trailing semicolon). This is strict and correct — but consider also accepting 'data:application/pdf,' (no media-type parameters) for completeness. Current callers always pass base64 form so this is theoretical.

useCustomerPage.js handlePreviewUploadedDoc still embeds `${dataUrl}` inside a DOMPurify.sanitize HTML string for image previews. The data URL is server-provided and passes through DOMPurify which validates http(s)/data:image schemes by default — acceptable, but using a React render (no innerHTML) would eliminate the templating altogether.

Interior email template does NOT use target=_blank on its CTA anchors — so the new noopener/noreferrer hook does not engage for that template. Not a bug (hook engages only when target=_blank is present), but if product wants CTAs to open in a new tab, the backend template should add target=_blank and the hook will then auto-harden the anchors.
